sanskrit: gaṇāvūcatuḥ | śivaśarmannudarkaṃ te kathayāvo niśāmaya | tvamatra vaiṣṇave loke bhuktvā bhogānsupuṣkalān || 1 || brahmaṇo vatsaraṃ pūrṇaṃ ramamāṇo'psarogaṇaiḥ | sutīrthamaraṇopātta puṇyaśeṣeṇa vai punaḥ || 2 || bhaviṣyasi mahīpālo nagare naṃdivardhane | rājyaṃ prāpyāsapatnaṃ ca samṛddhabalavāhanam || 3 ||
english: 1-4. O Śivaśarman, we shall speak what you are destined to have in future. Listen. Here in the world of Viṣṇu you will enjoy all pleasures in plenty. For the period of a year of Brahmā you will be sporting about with groups of celestial damsels. Due to the residue of the merit acquired by dying in an excellent holy place, you will become a king in the city of Nandivardhana. You will acquire a kingdom without any rivals or enemies. You will have plenty of vehicles and divisions of the army. In the kingdom, all the learned men will be hale and hearty. They will be having charming golden ornaments. The people there will perform regularly virtuous rites of Iṣṭa and Pūrta.
